claims.claim: The CDC estimates that each year roughly 1 in 6 Americans (about 48 million people) gets sick, 128,000 are hospitalized, and 3,000 die from foodborne diseases.

The FDA Food Code is a MODEL code: it is FDA's best advice offered for adoption by local, state, tribal, territorial, and federal jurisdictions, not a federal law that automatically binds every establishment; the 2022 edition is the 10th edition.

Under the Food Code, TCS food must be held at 135 F (57 C) or above when hot or at 41 F (5 C) or less when cold (Food Code 3-501.16); the range between these limits, about 41 F to 135 F, is the temperature danger zone where pathogens multiply.

Food Code 3-401.11 sets minimum cooking end-point temperatures: 145 F (63 C) for 15 seconds for fish, intact meat, and eggs cooked to order; 155 F (68 C) for 17 seconds for comminuted (ground) meat and similar non-intact foods; and 165 F (74 C) instantaneously for poultry and stuffed foods.
Food Code 3-501.14 requires cooked TCS food to be cooled from 135 F to 70 F within 2 hours and from 135 F to 41 F or less within a total of 6 hours.

The Food Code identifies six highly infectious 'Big 6' pathogens whose diagnosis in a food employee is reportable and triggers restriction or exclusion (Food Code 2-201.11): Norovirus, Hepatitis A virus, Shigella spp., Shiga toxin-producing E. coli (STEC), Typhoid fever (Salmonella Typhi), and nontyphoidal Salmonella.

The Food Code requires food employees to wash hands and exposed arms for at least 20 seconds at a handwashing sink (Food Code 2-301.12), and to protect food from cross-contamination by separating raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods during storage, preparation, holding, and display (Food Code 3-302.11).

Cleaning removes visible soil; sanitizing is a separate step that reduces microorganisms on a cleaned food-contact surface, achieved under the Food Code by hot-water immersion (at least 30 seconds manually, or a 160 F utensil surface temperature mechanically) or by an approved chemical sanitizer (Food Code 4-703.11).

The consumer-facing Clean / Separate / Cook / Chill framework organizes the four basic defenses against foodborne illness, and FoodSafety.gov recommends keeping the refrigerator at or below 40 F and discarding perishable food left in the danger zone for more than two hours (one hour above 90 F).

HACCP (Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point) is a preventive food-safety management system built on seven principles: (1) conduct a hazard analysis; (2) determine the critical control points; (3) establish critical limits; (4) establish monitoring procedures; (5) establish corrective actions; (6) establish verification procedures; (7) establish record-keeping and documentation procedures.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Whether 'the danger zone' is stated as 40 F to 140 F or 41 F to 135 F.
positions: Consumer USDA/FoodSafety.gov guidance often rounds the range to 40 F to 140 F for the general public.
The FDA Food Code, which governs retail and food-service establishments, uses 41 F (5 C) and 135 F (57 C) as the regulatory limits for cold and hot holding of TCS food.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson teaches the Food Code retail figures (41 F to 135 F) as the operational standard because the topic is foodservice, and notes that consumer guidance uses a slightly wider rounded range.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Whether the number of 'Big 6' pathogens is fixed.
positions: Older editions and some study guides list the six as of a particular Food Code edition.
The 2022 Food Code 2-201.11 enumerates six reportable diagnoses (Norovirus, Hepatitis A, Shigella, STEC, Salmonella Typhi, nontyphoidal Salmonella).
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson names the six exactly as listed in the 2022 Food Code text read directly, and attributes the list to Food Code 2-201.11 rather than to any proprietary curriculum.

unsupportedExistingClaims: The machine-generated draft was generic boilerplate ('Food Safety is a foundational concept...') containing no verifiable substance; it was treated as editorial intent only and discarded.
correctionsNeeded: Replaced placeholder definitions and vocabulary with Food Code-sourced numbers and terms.
Distinguished the retail Food Code danger-zone limits (41 F to 135 F) from rounded consumer guidance (40 F to 140 F).
Stated explicitly that the Food Code is a model code adopted variably by jurisdictions and that the lesson is not a substitute for a certified course or local compliance.
rightsIssues: All sources are U.S. federal government works (FDA, CDC, USDA FSIS, FoodSafety.gov) and are in the public domain; prose was nonetheless written originally and no source text was reproduced.

ServSafe and other proprietary food-handler curricula are copyrighted and were treated as REFERENCE_ONLY: they are not cited and none of their material was reproduced. The 'Big 6' concept is attributed to the FDA Food Code, its primary source.

sourceRecords.title: FDA Food Code 2022 (10th edition)
sourceRecords.notes: Primary model code. The full 736-page PDF (FDA /media/184685/download) was downloaded via curl with a browser user-agent and text-extracted locally with pypdf. Directly supports: model-code status and 10th-edition/2022 dating (landing page text: 'The Food Code is a model... offered for adoption by local, state, and federal governmental jurisdictions'); hot/cold holding 135 F / 41 F (3-501.16); cooking end-points 145/155/165 F with times (3-401.11); cooling 135 to 70 F in 2 h and 135 to 41 F in 6 h (3-501.14); Big 6 reportable diagnoses (2-201.11); 20-second handwash procedure (2-301.12); raw/ready-to-eat separation (3-302.11); sanitizing of food-contact surfaces (4-703.11). Public-domain U.S. government work; prose written originally.

Public-domain U.S. government work; only the principle names, which are standard terms of art, are used.

Used to corroborate cooking temperatures, not as the sole source.
